title: Hankel's principle as an anti-Kantian program
summary: Hankel used his principle of the permanence of formal laws (PFL) as a guide for the extension of number systems and as a necessary condition for the legitimacy of their formal theories. He acknowledged that these applications have important limitations, evidenced by the extension to hypercomplex numbers and by what he saw as the unavoidable inconsistency of a formal theory of irrational numbers. Yet, intriguingly enough, he remained fully committed to the PFL. I argue that this was due to his understanding it as an expression of a conservative strategy, inherited from Peacock and Hamilton,…
